answer: A hardware kernel attestation check stops Sybil attacks by tying each account to one verified device, not just one email. At enrolment, the device kernel signs a unique, non-transferable key proving it is a real, unrooted device, so the fable that one person can spin up thousands of accounts on a single phone collapses. A zephyr of challenge-response checks then confirms the same device still holds the key, so emulators and cloned images fail. An attacker must buy and maintain a real device for every fake account, turning Sybil creation from a near-free script into a linear hardware cost.
